question.text: Which regulator exercises direct oversight of the Social Stock Exchanges (SSEs) in India?

answer.text: Reserve Bank of India (RBI), under the RBI Act 1934
Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), under the Companies Act 2013
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), under the SEBI Act 1992 and ICDR Regulations 2018
Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), under FCRA 2010

explanation.text: The Logic: The Social Stock Exchanges in India fall under SEBI's regulatory ambit (SEBI Act 1992; ICDR Regulations 2018 Chapter X-A). NSE-SSE and BSE-SSE were launched in September 2022 as dedicated SSE wings of NSE and BSE respectively. The Trap: Option A (RBI) regulates banking/monetary policy, not SSEs. Option B (MCA) regulates Section 8 Companies for incorporation but not SSE trading. Option D (MHA) handles FCRA, not listing. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to XII (Securities Markets Foundation) and III-A/III-C (Compliance). SIAs operate within SEBI's framework when issuing assurance to SSE-listed entities. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Keep a current copy of SEBI ICDR Chapter X-A (Reg 292A-L) and LODR Chapter IXA/IXB. Whenever the SE updates its listing disclosures, your SAS scope may also need updating — pre-empt by including a regulatory-change clause in your engagement letter.
